about: Every number of the CuteAFD v5 page (docs/v5.html). Differences are second-named arm subtracted from the first-named ("hqa - anchor" above 0 = hqa scored higher). One engine, one model family, K4 experts and the same drafter in every arm: nothing here measures expert quantisation. Synthetic items; scores are not comparable with any other model family or fixture.

settings.items: 60 synthetic items (join, ledger, trace; 20 each), each rendered at 4K, 16K, 64K and 127K tokens (length labels 4k, 16k, 64k, 128k in the data); 8 answer fields per item
passes_per_arm: eight delivery turns then the question (turns-p8-rep0)
settings.sampling: thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k -1, one recorded seed per (item, length, pass): distinct within an arm, the same in every arm
settings.frozen: 2026-11-10 19:55:10, seven seconds before the first serving launch and before the first measured request (protocol/FROZEN.json); amendments: none for the graded runs of the three arms; amendment 1 of 2026-11-11 16:46 adds two single-message passes per arm, complete 2026-11-12 (protocol/AMENDMENT-2026-11-11.md; four_pass). The BF16-reference stage has its own plan, written 2026-11-11 17:54 before its first request (bf16ref/ADDENDUM-BF16REF.md; bf16_distance)

estimators.request_score: fields correct / fields, read from the last ANSWER: line; 0 if the reply did not finish with stop (reply cap or loop abort)
estimators.paired_difference_frozen_rule: per item, the mean over the shared (pass, length) requests of score(b) - score(a); the estimate is the mean over items; 95% interval: percentile over 10,000 resamples of the items (seed 5). Unit: the item (60; 20 for one family)
estimators.flip_share: share of (item, length) pairs whose every-field-right outcome differs: between two arms in the same pass (same seed), or between the two passes of one arm (the floor); p from an exact McNemar test
estimators.turns_minus_single: per item, eight-turn score minus the mean of the two single-message scores; interval as above
estimators.model_written_share: per eight-turn session: completion tokens of the delivery turns / prompt tokens of the final turn
estimators.post_hoc: 64K and 127K pooled; per item, mean over passes and the two lengths; plain item bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 7

turns.scope: Decode ran in every reply of every pass. What the 8-turn pass did not exercise is history written by decode: the model's own turns (thinking included, which stays in context) are a median 9% of the final prompt at 4K, 2.7% at 16K, 0.7% at 64K and 0.3-0.4% at 127K, so at long context more than 99% of the history the final answer was conditioned on was written by prefill. The pass measures split delivery of the same input. It does not test a conversation whose history the model wrote (protocol question 3). The turn design is to be revised.
turns.status: design to be revised; the protocol's advance reading ("turn check v2 not needed") is withdrawn

ledger_exploratory.note: by family, as the protocol asks of every table; outside the frozen comparison rule (plain item bootstrap, seed 20261111, indices 250 and 9750); 20 items

differences.note: by family, as the protocol asks of every table; outside the frozen comparison rule

ledger_exploratory.classifier: exploratory reading, not part of the frozen protocol: wrong answer fields on stop-finished `ledger` replies, by the kind of arithmetic slip the given value matches (heuristic: a wrong value can match a kind by coincidence)
ledger_exploratory.extension: held, not run (notes/ledger-extension-hold.md); its first trigger condition is met

post_hoc_long_context.note: post hoc; not in the frozen protocol; this section holds 48 intervals, of which two exclude 0

limits: speeds are per stream under a mixed concurrency-8 load and are not an arm comparison
open_questions: Where does the long-context loss that every probe arm shows, anchor included, come from? The arms share the model, the K4 experts, the engine, the drafter, the sampling settings and the reply cap; a third to a half of the loss is replies that did not finish.
Is the K6 core's nominal gap on long-context running totals (ledger at 64K and 127K) real? Twenty items leave both zero and a loss of about 0.13 in field score inside the pooled interval.
Is a conversation continued on history the model itself wrote equivalent to the same tokens prefilled? The eight-turn pass did not test this.

reference.about: Reference checkpoint added after the results were read; outside the frozen comparison, intervals post hoc. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. anchor stays the reference of the probe, not a recommendation.
reference.what: native EXLR8 checkpoint: routed and shared experts in a K4 trellis format with E4M3 rounding; attention output, q_b_proj and the dense MLP at K4; attention input projections MXFP8; embedding and head FP8
reference.loading: The engine loads a native EXLR8 checkpoint from a content-addressed store; for these launches the store (SparkNest v0.8.3, one node) ran on the same host and was mounted there.
reference.upstream_status: Upstream's status note says bundled vision and full prefix-continuation exactness are not yet qualified for this checkpoint, which is why it is run single-message only here.
reference.whole_checkpoint: exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component.
reference.ran: 2026-11-11 13:24 to 16:21, one launch per pass; no eight-turn pass

launch.source: each launch's server log; logs are not published

intervals.note: post hoc; six pairs x (field score at seven length groupings + every field right at six + ledger field score at 64K and 127K); no correction for the number of intervals

estimators.paired: as the frozen rule (per item, mean over the shared pass x length requests of score(b) - score(a); 10,000 resamples of the items, seed 5), applied to pairs that include the reference checkpoint
estimators.flip_floor: (item, length) pairs of 240 whose every-field-right outcome differs between the arm's own two passes
estimators.discordant: per pass, (item, length) pairs of 240 with every field right in the first-named arm only, then in the second-named arm only

capture.about: Exploratory, one capture per arm: the engine scores given texts (five texts, assistant frame, prefill and decode paths; nothing is sampled). Read beside the same capture of the three probe arms. No correction for the number of comparisons. Distance from the unquantized BF16 model is not measured by this capture: all four configurations are quantized (anchor has a BF16 core and K4 experts), so a difference from anchor is a difference from another quantization. Added 2026-11-12: that distance was measured afterwards in a separate stage, on two reference sets that reach 14.4K (bf16_distance; RESULTS.md section 12). against_text is referenced to the given text. between_arms is not a distance from the BF16 model: the three probe arms share their experts, so a distance between two of them reflects the settings outside the experts alone (the core and, for anchor, the output head), while exlr8-k4 has its own experts, so its distance to a probe arm includes both expert quantizations and does not rank it against the probe arms by closeness to the BF16 model. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component.

between_arms.kl: KL(first-named || second-named), nats, exact over the full vocabulary
between_arms.strata: by the lowest probability any arm gives the given token: sure >= 0.9, fair 0.5 to 0.9, unsure < 0.5 in every arm, mixed = the arms straddle 0.5

against_text.interval: 4000 resamples of runs of consecutive positions within each text, seed 20261110
against_text.collapse_rule: arm p < 0.05 and every other arm p >= 0.9

capture.source: exploratory/capture_pairs.json and exploratory/capture_abs.json; the dumps and per-row files they were computed from are not published

amendment_1.written_before: the first request of the passes it adds
amendment_1.adds: single-message passes 3 and 4 (single-rep2, single-rep3) for anchor, hqa, compact and exlr8-k4: same items, lengths, reply cap, concurrency and sampling settings, new seed blocks; the total is fixed at four single-message passes per arm before the first request of pass 3
amendment_1.rule: the frozen comparison rule applied to four passes; the two-pass tables stay as the result of the frozen protocol

four_pass.about: Amendment 1: four single-message passes per arm (RESULTS.md section 11). The frozen comparison rule applied to more passes; an extension decided after the two-pass results were read, with the total of four passes fixed before the first request of pass 3. Pass sets: p12 = passes 1-2 (the frozen protocol's result), p34 = passes 3-4 alone, p1234 = all four. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. anchor is the reference of the probe, not a recommendation.
four_pass.rule: request score = fields correct / fields if the reply finished with stop, else 0; repeats averaged within the item; b - a paired by item; 95% interval: percentile over 10,000 resamples of the items, seed 5. Unit: the item (60; 20 for one family)

intervals.expected_by_chance: at a 95% level about 5 of 102 would exclude 0 with no difference anywhere
intervals.note: six pairs x 17: field score at four lengths, all lengths and two length groups; every field right at four lengths, all lengths and 64K + 127K; ledger field score at 64K + 127K; field score in each of three families. No correction for the number of intervals; a single interval is not evidence on its own

single_pass_spread.note: largest difference between two of one arm's four single passes

descriptive_speed.note: median per stream under the mixed concurrency-8 load; descriptive, not an arm comparison under the protocol

four_pass.source: analysis/fourpass.py over analysis/samples.csv, analysis/samples-reference.csv and analysis/samples-extension.csv (python3 analysis/fourpass.py, standard library only) into analysis/FOURPASS.json

bf16_distance.about: Distance of each of the four configurations from the unquantized BF16 model, on two reference sets that hold BF16 outputs (RESULTS.md section 12). KL in nats; 0 is identical, lower is closer. Descriptive: no gate and no ranking rule; every interval computed is listed and none was selected. The two sets use different measures and are not comparable with each other. Neither reaches past 14.4K: the 64K and 127K lengths of the task runs have no BF16 reference here. Differences b - a: negative means b is closer to BF16. The three probe arms share their K4 experts, so a difference between two of them reflects the tensors outside the experts. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. anchor is the reference of the probe, not a recommendation.

fidelity_set.label: P-B
fidelity_set.source: the engine author's (tpurtell's) published fidelity set
fidelity_set.estimator: coarse KL, the engine author's rule (not full-vocabulary): per position, KL(BF16 reference || engine) in float64 over the reference's top 1,024 token ids plus one term for the rest of the vocabulary. Statistic: ratio of sums over generated positions (sum of per-position KL / number of positions). 95% interval: window-block bootstrap, 5,000 replicates, SplitMix64 seed 20260829; in each replicate one window is drawn per window, with replacement, in window order; 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles with linear interpolation. Unit: the window (53 with generated positions)
fidelity_set.estimator_paired: b - a on the same positions: (sum of per-position KL of b - that of a) / number of positions, with the same bootstrap and the same drawn windows for both arms
fidelity_set.recompute: fidelity_set_windows holds, per window, its positions and each arm's mean KL; positions x mean is the window's sum. Every fidelity-set value and interval of this file follows from that table with the estimator above (tools/verify.py does this for the findings that cite it)

teacher_panel.label: P-A
teacher_panel.source: published BF16 teacher logits for GLM 5.3 Flash
teacher_panel.estimator: full-vocabulary KL(BF16 teacher || engine) per row in float64, mean over rows. 95% interval: window bootstrap, 20,000 replicates, numpy default_rng(20260929), percentile. Unit: the window (25)
teacher_panel.estimator_paired: b - a per row on the same rows, mean over rows, same bootstrap
teacher_panel.recompute: teacher_panel_windows holds, per window, its rows and each arm's mean KL; the overall value is the row-weighted mean. The interval needs numpy's generator (repro/stage0/scorers/score_pa.py)
teacher_panel.note: drawn from the corpus the K4 producer published and can favour the K4 experts the three probe arms carry

intervals.note: six pairs x (fidelity set overall and three buckets, teacher panel); no correction for the number of intervals
